A liver transplant is a life-saving surgical procedure for end-stage liver disease, cirrhosis, liver cancer, or acute liver failure. A healthy liver from a living donor or deceased donor replaces the diseased liver to restore normal liver function. Liver transplant surgery improves quality of life, enhances survival, and offers a long-term solution for liver failure patients.

A kidney transplant is a major surgical procedure for treating end-stage kidney failure or chronic kidney disease. A healthy kidney from a living donor or deceased donor is implanted into a recipient whose kidneys no longer function properly. The new kidney is connected to blood vessels and the bladder to filter blood, produce urine, and maintain fluid and electrolyte balance. Kidney transplant surgery improves quality of life, reduces or eliminates the need for dialysis, and regulates blood pressure. Recipients require lifelong immunosuppressive therapy to prevent organ rejection. Kidney transplant treatment offers a long-term, life-saving solution for renal failure.

The bone marrow is a vital tissue where all blood cells are formed from stem cells. These stem cells differentiate into red blood cells (erythrocytes), carrying oxygen throughout the body, and white blood cells (leukocytes), supporting the immune system. Bone marrow transplant is a life-saving procedure for patients with blood disorders such as aplastic anemia, leukemia, lymphoma, thalassemia, and multiple myeloma. During the procedure, diseased marrow is replaced with healthy donor bone marrow or autologous stem cells to regenerate normal blood cell production. Successful stem cell transplantation restores immune function, improves oxygen delivery, and can put patients with blood cancer into remission. Advanced bone marrow transplant treatments offer effective, long-term solutions for hematologic disorders, providing renewed health, improved survival, and a chance for a normal, healthy life.

The anterior cruciate ligament is a vital tissue in the knee joint that connects bones and provides stability. A bilateral total knee replacement (B/L) is performed when both knees require surgical replacement. During surgery, the damaged portion of the femur is replaced with a metal component, while the tibial surface is fitted with a metal and high-grade plastic implant. In some cases, an artificial kneecap is also used. The joint’s cruciate ligaments, including the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) and posterior cruciate ligament (PCL), may be preserved or substituted, with the PCL sometimes replaced by a durable polyethylene post.

Shock wave lithotripsy (SWL) is a non-invasive kidney stone treatment designed to break kidney stones and ureter stones without surgery. There are two main techniques. The first involves the patient lying in a tub of lukewarm water while an X-ray or ultrasound imaging precisely locates the stone. The technician delivers targeted shock waves to fragment the stone. The second, more common method, uses a cushioned table that allows high-energy shock waves to penetrate the body directly. Using 1,000–2,000 shock waves, the stones are broken into smaller fragments, which pass naturally through the urinary tract. Lithotripsy treatment is safe, effective, and performed under local anesthesia, general anesthesia, or sedation. With minimal side effects and low complication rates, shock wave lithotripsy is a preferred kidney stone removal procedure. This advanced urology treatment provides rapid relief and avoids invasive surgery, improving patient outcomes.
